title: Modi Tells SCO Summit 'No Place for Double Standards' on Terrorism, in Veiled Message to Pakistan
detail: Addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on September 1, 2026 — in the presence of Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif — Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said 'we must speak in one voice that there can be no place for double standards in dealing with terrorism,' and called on member states to 'dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.' Modi did not name Pakistan directly, but analysts described the remarks, plus a separate line stressing that connectivity projects 'must fully respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all nations,' as a dual veiled jibe at Islamabad (over cross-border terrorism) and Beijing (over the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, which runs through Pakistan-administered Kashmir). Modi also argued 'there is no solution on the battlefield and all wars and conflicts should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy.' Neither Sharif nor Pakistani officials issued an on-record rebuttal at the summit itself.

confidenceReason: On-record summit remarks confirmed by multiple Tier-2 Indian outlets quoting the same speech text.
